description: An eight-storey, forty-unit encapsulated mass timber apartment design leaves two opposite-facing CLT wall surfaces exposed inside each suite. Together they are 20% of the suite perimeter-wall area and have a stated flame-spread rating of 100. All ceilings, beams and columns remain encapsulated. We want the opposite walls exposed without adding protection.
known_facts: two opposite-facing CLT wall surfaces exposed
exposed walls total 20% of perimeter-wall area

missing_info.field: owner or representative contact and property identification
risk assessment, mitigating measures, assumptions and supporting documents
missing_info.why: Alternative-path completeness items; request evidence rather than fabricate a professional conclusion.

gold.departure: Opposite-facing mass timber wall surfaces are left unencapsulated rather than meeting the exposed-wall exception.

should_cite.why: The exposed-wall exception requires surfaces to face the same direction.
The area ceiling is a separate condition; meeting it does not remove the direction condition.

must_not_cite.why: The exposed surfaces face opposite directions.

gold.engineering_reason: The stated occupancy, building size or dwelling count is outside the Division C exemption; applicable drawings require qualified registered professionals.
